To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the transition from a “monopolized” to a “distributed” model for knowledge production and distribution requires new institutional arrangements between HEIs and work places, and (ii) these institutional arrangements need to build on a new model for learning that is based on a “socially distributed commons.”
the symbiotic learning system is a strategy to deal with institutional challenges posed by an emergent transition from “social monopolized” to socially distributed knowledge generation and learning.

the concept of symbiotic learning systems is a useful strategy for addressing the problems and opportunities posed by a transition from a socially monopolized to a socially distributed model of knowledge production and learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a new conceptual framework for a more integrated and effective learning system, where the knowledge production of research, higher education and vocational education is integrated into the knowledge distribution and application in the work place.
how the relationship between HEIs and work places can be improved in the future by reorganizing the division of labor, responsibilities, and learning efforts between them.
the development of new organizational and institutional arrangements that can help HEIs and work organizations to learn from each other and to develop new forms of learning in work life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

symbiotic learning systems can be seen as the next step in the development of the relationship between HEIs and work life, and that the general preconditions of learning can be seen as a necessary foundation of such a relationship.

the concept of symbiotic learning systems is a promising strategy for dealing with the institutional knowledge and learning challenge posed by the transition from “social monopolies of knowledge” to “social distributions of learning” in a world of “learning organizations.”

the symbiotic learning systems approach offers a promising way forward for the future relationship between higher education institutions and the world of work, and that the symbiotic approach can contribute to the development of new forms of knowledge production and knowledge distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have tried to show the importance of a more general understanding of learning and learning systems, and how the development of such systems may be a precondition for the establishment of a more effective and sustainable relationship between HEIs and work life.
the “symbiotic” relationship between HEIs and work places can be seen as a new way to organize and integrate learning efforts and responsibilities in the emerging knowledge economy.

the concept of symbiotic learning systems is a way of addressing the challenges of the emerging knowledge society, and of building foundations for a new and improved relationship between work life and institutions for higher education and research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning is a process in which the individual and the social are intertwined.
learning in the future will be a much more social and interactive phenomenon than it is today.
the concept of “synchronic learning systems” may serve as a basis for reorganizing and integrating learning efforts and responsibilities between HEIs and work places.
